title: Bad restrictions force a canonical path of length $d$
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables, let $\rho$ be a restriction of those variables, and let $d$ be a natural number. Suppose $\rho$ is bad for $f$ at depth $d$: the restriction $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ of the Boolean function computed by $f$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $d$. Then the deepest root-to-leaf path of the canonical decision tree of $f$ under $\rho$, truncated to its first $d$ steps, is a sequence of exactly $d$ pairs (queried variable, branch direction) — equivalently, that path has length at least $d$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
ρ is a restriction on n variables
ρ is bad for f at depth d, i.e. the restricted function of f has decision-tree depth greater than d
